smell: The codebase still leans on the `prefix: message` convention ('update-ingress:', 'haproxy:', 'kubevip:', 'cluster:', 'cleanup:', 'terraform:', 'coreos:', 'iso:', 'csr:', 'addons:') in message bodies, but no call-site pins a structured `component` or `phase` attr via logger.With(). Only `run_id` is propagated (tui.SetRunID). JSON consumers can filter by run_id but cannot filter `component=haproxy` because no such key ever reaches the record. A grep for `Log.With("phase"`/`Log.With("component"` returns zero matches across the repo.
evidence:
p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("update-ingress: waiting for %s loadbalancer ip", svcName))
p.Log.Info("haproxy: removing configuration")
logger.Warn("cleanup: failed to stop service", "svc", serviceName, "err", err)
// 130 prefix-in-message sites across 21 files; zero `.With("phase"|"component")` pinning
severity_reason: Pervasive field-stability issue — blocks JSON log filtering by component; run_id correlation narrows practical impact. Not correctness.
fix_summary: At each phase constructor (setup/install/postinstall/destroy/cleanup) wrap p.Log via logger.With("phase", "install"); at sub-component boundaries (haproxy, dns, kubevip, terraform, iso, packages, cleanup.services, cleanup.packages, addon.manager) narrow with logger.With("component", "haproxy"). Retain the human prefix in the message for TTY readability — the attr is additive. WithAttrs propagates through RedactHandler.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: stable keys, per-component WithAttrs
Google SRE, Structured Logging — 'fields are for machines, messages for humans'
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/helpers.go:L194 — tui.Info("starting deployment...", tui.LF("cluster", clusterFQDN)) uses the correct attr shape
must_preserve: Operator-visible prefix for TTY readability; existing run_id pinned attr.

smell: Orchestrator.executeStep still does not emit a structured start/finish log pair per step. Skipping is logged (L90) but success/duration is not — Duration is captured in StepResult but never reaches the logger. Each phase's steps.go hand-rolls uneven OnStart/OnComplete log lines, so JSON consumers see inconsistent span boundaries. For a 60-minute install, missing per-step duration hurts post-mortem debugging. A grep for 'step started'/'step completed' returns zero matches.
severity_reason: Debuggability gap — missing per-step duration in structured stream. Not correctness.
fix_summary: In executeStep, before step.OnStart() log `o.logger.Info("step started", "step", step.ID(), "name", step.Name())`. After Execute (both success and error branches) log `o.logger.Info("step completed", "step", step.ID(), "duration", time.Since(startedAt), "success", err == nil)`. Keep at Debug if operator feedback finds Info too chatty — OnStart/OnComplete already emit TTY-oriented lines.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: span boundaries at orchestration layer
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/orchestrator.go:L90 — skip branch already logs structurally
must_preserve: Existing step.OnStart / step.OnComplete hand-rolled lines — new lines are additive.

smell: configureLogging still does not auto-select JSON format when stderr is not a TTY. Operators piping `okdctl deploy 2>&1 | jq .` get charmlog text with ANSI escapes by default and must remember `--log-format json`. Progress-bar suppression IS TTY-aware (L59-L64) and NO_COLOR is honored for progress, so the template for the fix exists in the same function — just extend it to logFormat.
severity_reason: UX affordance; operators can pass --log-format json explicitly. Prior audit's findings stand.
fix_summary: Route cobra's cmd into configureLogging so `cmd.Flags().Changed("log-format")` is available. If not set and !stderrIsTTY, default logFormat to "json". Explicit --log-format wins. Alternatively keep text but disable ANSI when !stderrIsTTY by exposing a charmlog color-profile toggle from tui.ConfigureLoggers. The progressBars gate at L64 is the template.
rule_source: CLI UX convention: auto-switch to machine format when piped
Go log/slog design: handler selection at main
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/logging.go:L59-L64 — the TTY-aware gate already exists for progress bars
must_preserve: --log-format flag takes precedence over auto-detection; --quiet/--verbose log-level sugar.

smell: secretstore.installPrereqCheck still logs multi-line HOW-TO guides (onepassword: 6 Warn lines, vault: 3 Warn lines, bitwarden: 3 Warn lines) via env.Logger.Warn when credential files are missing. Warn is for recoverable degradation; this is user education. Structured log sinks (JSON / file) record 6+ Warn entries per missing provider that an alerting rule will count as six distinct issues.
evidence:
env.Logger.Warn(fmt.Sprintf("secretstore: no secret files found in %s, skipping", dir))
env.Logger.Warn("secretstore: to set up 1password connect secrets:")
env.Logger.Warn("  1. download 1password-credentials.json from Settings > Automation in 1password.com")
env.Logger.Warn("  2. create a connect token and save it:")
// ... 4 more env.Logger.Warn lines
severity_reason: Level-discipline — Warn misused for help text, duplicated per-provider. Not correctness.
fix_summary: Emit the first line ('no secret files found ... skipping') at Warn as the actual advisory. Print numbered instructions via tui.Info (or fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, ...)) — operator-facing setup guidance belongs on the UX channel, not the structured log. Same pattern for vault and bitwarden.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: Warn for recoverable degradation, Info for state, fmt/tui for user UX
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/helpers.go — setup hints go through tui.Info, not env.Logger.Warn
must_preserve: The help content — move channel, don't lose it.

smell: coreos.go logs `coreos: found existing iso at X` (L59, L73) and `coreos: iso already exists at X` (L201, L265) in four distinct sites. A single setup run can fire more than one because the lookups happen across different layers (local iso dir, work-dir cache, download destination, upload destination), producing near-identical Info lines. Same event announced repeatedly as each caller layer does its own existence check.
severity_reason: Signal-to-noise; same event logged multiple times per run.
fix_summary: Consolidate the four sites into one helper (`logISOFound(path)`) that emits the Info line once per iso-path in a run — keep a set of already-logged paths keyed off filepath.Base. If the two message variants (found vs already-exists) carry distinct operator semantics, rename them so the distinction is legible.
rule_source: Google SRE, Structured Logging: log-once-per-event
Go proverb: clear is better than clever
must_preserve: Either variant's diagnostic value — operator wants to see the iso was found, but not three times per setup.

smell: The prior audit flagged three terraform count-in-message lines in proxmox.go; L158 and L185 are now structured (`"count", n`) but L217 remains `fmt.Sprintf("terraform: plan will preview %d virtual machines", totalNodes)`. The pattern also spreads to cleanup/summary.go L73 / L80 / L94 and addon/manager.go L78 / L101 / L117 / L125 / L181 — numeric counts wedged into the message string that JSON consumers cannot index by `count`. Scope has widened from the prior finding.
severity_reason: Field-stability — numeric fields wedged into message string. Partial resolution widened the gap's visibility to cleanup/summary and addon/manager.
fix_summary: Replace the remaining `fmt.Sprintf(...%d...)` log sites with structured attrs: proxmox.go:L217 → `p.logger.Info("terraform: plan preview", "vm_count", totalNodes)`; cleanup/summary.go:L73/L80/L94 → match L67's shape `logger.Info("cleanup: ignition files", "count", n)`; addon/manager.go:L78/L101/L117/L125/L181 → `"addons: installing", "count", len(ordered)` etc. Keep human prefix in the message for TTY readability.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: typed attrs for machine consumers
repo-counter-example: internal/infrastructure/proxmox/proxmox.go:L158,L185 — already migrated in this run
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/cleanup/summary.go:L67 — correct shape beside L73's incorrect one
must_preserve: The human prefix (terraform:, addons:, cleanup:) for TTY users.

smell: MonitorInstallation's CSR approval tick runs every 30s for up to 60 minutes. On each tick: on error it Warns structured, on approved>0 it Infos structured. The error case correctly logs every tick (diagnostic value) but during a prolonged CSR endpoint outage the Warn stream can reach ~120 entries, all identical in root cause. This is the log-per-retry pattern at Warn level.
severity_reason: Bounded at 2 Warns/minute. Keeping as suggestion: during a genuine outage you want to see repeated failures, and de-duping risks hiding a slow-degrading endpoint.
fix_summary: Optional: de-dup identical consecutive Warns via a `lastWarnErrMsg` tracker, downgrading repeats to Debug after the first. Keep `approved>0` Info as-is (state transition). Only apply if operator feedback actually reveals noise.
rule_source: Google SRE, Monitoring: log state changes, not constant failures
Go proverb: clear is better than clever
must_preserve: approved>0 Info — operators rely on seeing progress.

smell: executor.run and RunInteractive still only log `+ <name> <args>` at Debug when Verbose is true — nothing bookends the call in the structured stream. For a 15-minute terraform apply or oc poll the JSON sink sees nothing until completion. Cross-ref: prior-wave subprocess audit flagged buffered terraform output; observability owns the span-boundary half.
severity_reason: Operator feedback gap for JSON/file sinks; TTY is covered by spinner. Not correctness.
fix_summary: At start of executor.run log `e.logger.Debug("exec started", "cmd", name, "argc", len(args))` (omit argv itself — terraform invocation argv can contain a credential substitution in rare configs). After cmd.Run log `e.logger.Debug("exec completed", "cmd", name, "exit", result.ExitCode, "duration", result.Duration)`. Keep at Debug so default verbosity is unchanged.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: span boundaries
seam: subprocess audit
must_preserve: The Verbose-gated `+ name args` Debug line.

smell: The ctx-done-miss branch at L120 was migrated to structured form `tui.Error("command failed", tui.LF("err", err))` — prior audit's core case. The SetFlagErrorFunc handler at L187 still stringifies: `tui.Error(err.Error())`. Once tui.X routes through RedactHandler (already done), stringifying a cobra flag-parse error preempts the handler's walk; structured form lets Redacted()-implementing wrapped errors survive the sink. Narrower scope than prior run.
severity_reason: Last remaining top-level stringification. Cobra flag errors are unlikely to carry credentials, so downgraded from minor to suggestion after the L120 fix.
fix_summary: Replace `tui.Error(err.Error())` with `tui.Error("flag error", tui.LF("err", err))`. Keep the exit-code logic unchanged. Once tui.X routes through RedactHandler, passing err as attr lets the handler apply redactAny.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: pass errors as structured attrs
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/root.go:L120 — the companion site was already fixed
seam #3 — observability owns the sink half

smell: destroy.steps.go builds its per-step OnError callback as `phase.WarnOnError(p.Log, label+": "+err.Error())(err)`, which concatenates err.Error() into the Warn message AND passes err again as the structured attr (WarnOnError body: `logger.Warn(msg, "err", err)`). Result: the error text appears twice — once inlined into `msg` (bypassing RedactHandler's attr-walk) and once as the structured `err` attr. The inlined copy pre-empties redaction because RedactHandler only rewrites attr values, not the free-form message.
severity_reason: Field-stability + redaction-sink overlap: double-logs the error and the inlined copy bypasses RedactHandler. Low blast radius today because the destroy path's errors don't carry credentials in practice, but the pattern is structurally wrong.
fix_summary: Drop the `+ ": " + err.Error()` concatenation: `phase.WarnOnError(p.Log, label)(err)`. WarnOnError already emits `logger.Warn(label, "err", err)`, which gives structured consumers the label and a redaction-eligible err attr. TTY users still see `label err=<err>` formatted by charmlog.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets — 'attrs go through RedactHandler'
Go log/slog idiom: err as attr, not embedded in msg
seam #3 — observability owns the sink
must_preserve: The failures slice append and the call to WarnOnError(p.Log, msg)(err) — only the concat is removed.
